ideas.pitch: An AI-powered routing platform for Cincinnati workers that optimizes public transit commutes using METRO schedule data combined with real-time shift openings in high-growth local manufacturing and healthcare hubs.
ideas.title: Cincinnati Transit Equity & Job Access Router
ideas.why_it_could_win: Targets concrete social impact and local relevance for Cincinnati judges, mirroring the proven pattern of solving real regional accessibility problems.

ideas.pitch: An emergency response coordination dashboard that uses synthetic computer vision streams to aggregate and classify campus safety incidents, providing first responders with automated geofenced risk assessments.
ideas.title: Campus Safety AI Drone Dispatch Monitor
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solves a problem the judges feel themselves on a university campus, making the utility immediately apparent during live judging.

ideas.pitch: An autonomous forecasting tool for Cincinnati small businesses and food trucks that predicts weekly inventory needs using localized event schedules and weather data to streamline micro-financing approvals.
ideas.title: Local Vendor Micro-Loan & Inventory Predictor
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines predictive analytics with clear economic impact, following the exact formula of successful forecasting and risk-assessment hackathon winners.

ideas.pitch: An AI agent ecosystem that models IoT sensor streams along the Ohio River basin to forecast heavy metal spikes and chemical runoff anomalies before municipal systems detect them.
ideas.title: Ohio River Watershed Water Quality Forecasting Agent
ideas.why_it_could_win: Applies rigorous time-series forecasting to an environmental issue specific to the local geography of the Ohio River valley.

ideas.pitch: A decentralized project registry and collaboration platform that uses smart contracts to protect student intellectual property and securely match student builders with regional sponsor companies.
ideas.title: Student Hackathon Project IP Escrow & Matching Engine
ideas.why_it_could_win: Targets the exact ecosystem of university hackathons, solving a persistent pain point around project continuation and IP management after the event ends.
